- When sentiment is low (≤0.3) and forecast drops sharply, model tends to underestimate — correct by adding 1–2% to forecasted values.
- After a price spike, model often overshoots in the next 5–7 days — apply a 1–3% downward correction to avoid overreaction.
- If sentiment is high (≥0.6) and forecast is rising, model frequently overestimates — reduce forecast by 1–2% to align with mean reversion.
- Model consistently underestimates in the first 3–5 days of a new trend — adjust downward by 0.5–1.5% for early horizon.
- When sentiment is volatile (fluctuating 0.3–0.7) and price is near recent low, model tends to lag — forecast should be slightly ahead of true price by 1–2 days.
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 50% of 30d average), model overreacts — reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 3–5 days.
- For long-term (30d) forecasts, if sentiment is neutral or slightly negative, model often overcorrects — apply a 0.5–1.5% downward bias to avoid overoptimism.
